reason: This passage from Genesis 4 recounts the story of Cain and Abel, two individual brothers. While Cain does express a complaint to God—specifically stating that his iniquity/punishment is too great to bear (וַיֹּ֥אמֶר קַ֖יִן אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל עֲוֺנִ֖י מִנְּשֹֽׂא)—this is a personal lament about his own divine punishment, not a collective complaint by the Hebrew people about their leaders. The text makes no reference to the Hebrew people as a group or to any form of leadership; it is instead a primordial narrative about familial conflict and divine justice at the beginning of human history.
